lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 3 of Unit 2: Shapes and Spaces! Today, we are going to dive deeper into the exciting world of shapes. We will learn about two-dimensional shapes such as circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles. These shapes are all around us, in buildings, toys, and nature! 

First, let's start with a fun song about shapes. Gather around and sing along as we point out the different shapes we've learned so far. (Feel free to make up actions for each shape to make it even more fun!) After our song, we will have a little discussion about where we see these shapes in our everyday lives. For instance, a pizza is a circle, a book is a rectangle, and our school windows are often squares. 

Next, we will explore how these shapes can come together to make new shapes. For example, when you put two triangles together, they can form a square! We will use our bodies for this activity, where students will stand up to represent different shapes and work together to build new shapes with their bodies. This physical engagement helps reinforce their understanding of shapes and encourages teamwork. 

Finally, to wrap up our lesson, we will take a moment to listen to a story that includes various shapes. As we read, I'll pause and ask questions about the shapes we see in the illustrations. This will help students relate our lesson to literature and observe that shapes are not only in the classroom but also in stories! This creative exploration of shapes will make them excited and curious about the world around them.
interactive_assignment: For today's hands-on activity, we are going to create a 'Shape City'! Each student will receive various pre-cut shapes from colored paper, including squares, circles, triangles, and rectangles. Your task is to design a city using these shapes on a large piece of construction paper. You can make buildings, roads, and parks by combining different shapes. Once everyone has completed their artwork, we will share our Shape City creations with the class. Be prepared to explain which shapes you used and where they are located in your city!
